subject: Diffferent results with ezANOVA and SPSS 19

messages.author: 0880ba6874ca97df
messages.subject: Diffferent results with ezANOVA and SPSS 19
parts:
Hi,

when I calculate a mixed model ANOVA (1WS and 1BS, slighly unbalanced
sample, Type III) the way it is explayned here:
http://egret.psychol.cam.ac.uk/statistics/R/anova.html#technicalities
I get different results whith R and ez than in SPSS19.

I use the following codes on the same data (just reshaped to wide
format of the WS-variable in SPSS):

### R:
anova = ezANOVA(
data = dat
, dv = .(Bewertung)
, wid = .(Pb)
, within = .(Situation)
, between = .(Konzept)
, type = 3
, detailed = T
)

### SPSS:
DATASET ACTIVATE DatenSet1.
GLM Angemessen..Anzeige..2 Angemessen..Anzeige..3 Angemessen..Anzeige..
4 BY Konzept
/WSFACTOR=Situation 3 Polynomial
/METHOD=SSTYPE(1)
/CRITERIA=ALPHA(.05)
/WSDESIGN=Situation
/DESIGN=Konzept.

Has someone an idea, what could be the reason?

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Diffferent results with ezANOVA and SPSS 19
parts:
I'm not familiar with SPSS, but "SSTYPE(1)" sounds like you're asking
it for type 1 sums of squares, but in your call to ezANOVA, you're
asking for type 3.

messages.subject: Re: [ez4r] Diffferent results with ezANOVA and SPSS 19
parts:
Hi - sorry - it was the wrong SPSS-Code. But the results are different
with SSTYPE(3), too.
In R I found a solution using the following code in the car-package:

summary(Anova(lm(formula = cbind(Sit1, Sit2, Sit3) ~ Konzept, data=dat),
idata = data.frame(Situation = factor(1:3)),
idesign = ~Situation,
type = "III"))

There I get the same results like SSTYPE(3). So I'm fine with this solution,
but thank you very much for the quick response!!!
Felix
